title: brazil-smb-field-activation-brief
body:
Purpose:
This is a field-facing activation brief for the Brazil SMB launch (PT-BR).
It bundles positioning, competitor notes, sales playbook bullets, sample announcement copy (EN/PT), and an enablement checklist for SDRs, AEs, and Solutions Engineers.

TL;DR:
- Objective: Drive first 50 paying SMB customers in Brazil in Q2 post-GA; enable 30 sales/solutions reps with localized content and demos.
- Headline message: High-performance LLM inference for Brazilian teams — predictable latency, lower token costs, and a simple path from POC to private deployment with LGPD-ready controls.

Target audience / personas (Brazil SMB focus):
- Product Lead at fast-moving SaaS startup (10–150 employees) needing chat/summary features with predictable inferencing costs.
- Engineering lead at growth-stage marketplace who cares about latency and easy rollout across regions.
- Platform/IT manager at small enterprise (regulated fintech/healthtech) who needs data locality and compliance (LGPD).

Positioning & message hierarchy:
1) Primary headline (EN): "Predictable, production-grade LLM inference for Brazilian teams."
1a) PT-BR headline: "Inferência de LLM em produção, com latência e custo previsíveis para equipes no Brasil."
2) Supporting points (short):
- Latency and region control: Sao Paulo region and routing policies keep chat latency <200ms median for local apps.
- Cost controls: batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization recommendations tuned to common SMB prompts reduces token spend by 20–40%.
- Compliance-ready: private deployment and KMS integrations to support LGPD and customer data isolation needs.

Top three benefits (one-liners for sales):
- Ship features faster: same API across hosted, dedicated, and private so devs iterate without infra changes.
- Predictable economics: tooling to recommend batching/quantization so customers scale without surprise bills.
- Enterprise-grade fallback: model routing and automatic fallbacks keep core UX online during capacity events.

Competitive snapshot (field notes - quick read):
- Hypothetical competitors in Brazil SMB space: large hyperscalers' managed endpoints (AWS/Azure/GCP), regional MSPs offering managed LLM endpoints, and a handful of local startups packaging inference.
- Strengths vs hyperscalers: more transparent per-token economics, opinionated inference controls (batching, cache), simplified rollout from hosted to private for regulated customers.
- Weaknesses: brand awareness in Brazil is lower than hyperscalers; we may need strong reference customers and technical proof points.
- Key threats: cloud promotions from hyperscalers (free credits), MSPs bundling inference with existing managed services (one-stop shops).

Pricing positioning for SMBs:
- Emphasize predictable unit economics rather than lowest headline price. Use example cost comparisons for a 10k DAU chat app showing cost savings from caching + batching.
- Offer a limited-time "Brazil SMB starter" package: 3 months reduced platform fee + onboarding credit for the first 20 customers. (Ops to confirm).

Localized considerations (PT-BR):
- Tone: pragmatic, engineering-focused but friendly. Avoid hyperbole.
- Translate technical terms carefully (e.g., "latency" -> "latência", "batching" -> "aglutinação de requisições" or keep as "batching" in parentheses).
- Legal: mention LGPD and data residency options explicitly.

Sales playbook (one-page cheatsheet):
- Lead qualification checklist:
  - Use case: chat, summarization, embeddings search, personalization?
  - Data sensitivity: PII/financial/health? If yes -> private/dedicated conversation.
  - Latency requirement: <300ms? push region and routing SLOs.
  - Budget: monthly token spend estimate > $X -> discuss Dedicated.
- Demo script (5–10 mins):
  1) Quick intro + customer problem.
  2) Live call to hosted API showing PT-BR prompt -> 2–3 outputs streaming to show latency.
  3) Show Console: token cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, model rollout.
  4) Walkthrough of Dedicated/private options and LGPD controls.
- Objection handling:
  - "Hyperscalers are cheaper": show real token-unit economics and caching/batching impact.
  - "We have vendor lock-in concerns": highlight same API across deployment types and exportable model pinning.
  - "We need data residency": explain Redwood Private and VPC/on-prem options plus KMS integrations.

Enablement assets (to produce/localize):
- PT-BR one-pager: product benefits + pricing example (1 page).
- Sales deck (10 slides) with local market stats and two Brazil SME case studies (template).
- Technical quickstart repo: PT-BR README + sample Node/Python prompts for common SMB flows.
- Live demo script & recorded walkthroughs (hosted API + Dedicated conversion).
- Battlecard: competitor dos/ don'ts and pricing comparison.
- FAQ doc in PT-BR for Support/CS.

Go-to-market channels and tactics for early traction:
- Developer-first outreach: localized quickstart repo + targeted Twitter/X threads + Portuguese blog post about latency optimizations for PT-BR models.
- Partner plays: engage 3 local consultancies/MSPs to build referral demos (revenue share pilot).
- Events: sponsor two local meetups in SP (AI & Cloud) and host a technical workshop.
- Beta cohort: invite 10 startups from accelerator partners for free onboarding credits and publish 2 case studies.

Sample announcement copy (short, EN):
Subject: "Now available in Brazil: low-latency, cost-aware LLM inference"
Body (EN): "Redwood Inference is available in Sao Paulo, offering predictable latency, cost controls, and LGPD-ready deployment paths for Brazilian teams. Try our quickstart and see how batching and caching can reduce your token costs while improving latency."

Sample announcement copy (short, PT-BR):
Assunto: "Agora no Brasil: inferência LLM com baixa latência e controle de custos"
Corpo (PT-BR): "O Redwood Inference está disponível em São Paulo, com latência previsível, controles de custo e opções de implantação compatíveis com LGPD. Experimente nosso quickstart e veja como batching e cache reduzem gasto por token mantendo a latência baixa."

Longer press-style paragraph (PT-BR):
"Redwood Inference lança operação na região de São Paulo com uma plataforma dedicada a tornar inferência de modelos de linguagem escalável e previsível para equipes brasileiras. A solução oferece rotas por política, caching de prefixos e recomendações de quantização para reduzir custos operacionais, além de opções de implantação privada para clientes com requisitos de conformidade e residência de dados (LGPD)."

Launch timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (Mar 10): Enablement packet finalized; assets translated to PT-BR.
- Week 1 (Mar 17): Internal all-hands demo + recorded walkthrough distributed.
- Week 2 (Mar 24): Beta invites out to 10 startups and partners.
- Week 6 (Apr 21): Public GA announcement and localized site launch.

Success metrics (first 90 days post-GA):
- 50 paying SMB customers in Brazil.
- 30 trained reps with completed enablement quiz (score >80%).
- 2 public case studies published.
- Median chat latency <200ms for PT-BR sample workload for 80% of customers.

Operational/Risk notes:
- Support readiness: ensure Brazilian Portuguese CS triage and escalation docs ready before GA.
- Pricing confusion: prepare calculators and 1:1 cost run sessions for the top 10 pipeline deals.
- Capacity planning: coordinate with infra/serving-runtime to confirm Sao Paulo region GPU capacity and fallback routing for peak times.

Action items (owners):
- Sales: Priya Nair -> finalize beta invite list and outreach script.
- Solutions Eng: Lucas Ferreira -> prepare two live demos and quickstart repo.
- Marketing: Sophie Martin -> finalize PT-BR one-pager and blog post.
- Product/Infra: Ethan Kim -> confirm regional capacity & fallback policy.

Appendix: localized sample prompts (PT-BR) for demo flows:
- Customer support summary: "Resuma a conversa do cliente e extraia três intenções principais."
- Short-form generation: "Gere um email curto em PT-BR para reengajar usuários inativos com tom profissional e 2 opções de assunto."
- Embeddings search sample: use Portuguese content snippet to show similarity scoring and how embeddings surface localized results.

Notes to field: treat this as living doc; add wins, pricing objections encountered, and any local partner leads to the Confluence page linked above.

End of brief.
